items.heading: "I Want to Switch"
items.text: "I want to switch" is not one decision for an IT professional. It is at least five different moves, and each one has a different risk, cost, and timeline. Most bad switches happen because someone applied a company-switch mindset to what was really a domain switch, or vice versa.

items.heading: This Is the Step Almost
items.text: This is the step almost everyone skips, and it is the one that turns a clean switch into a messy one. Before you send a single application, pull out your actual offer letter or appointment terms and read the exit clause word for word.

items.heading: Somewhere Between Your Resignation
items.text: Somewhere between your resignation and your last working day, a counter-offer is a real possibility, especially if you are senior, mid-career, or hard to replace quickly. Decide how you will respond before that conversation happens, not in the room.

items.heading: A Counter
items.text: A counter-offer buys the company time to plan a transition on its own schedule instead of yours.

items.heading: IT Rarely Reflects a Sudden
items.text: It rarely reflects a sudden realisation of your value; it reflects the cost and disruption of losing you right now.
